positive.response: Preserve the successful visible workflow and its original evidence. Independent verification now confirms all five saved projects, exact 30.000-second WAVs and MIDI exports, full saved-graph sample-exact reproduction, and actual audio/VST contributions through separate source ablations. This does not establish heard musical quality, sustained live playback reliability, physical-device behavior or broader plug-in compatibility.

duplicate_tool.response: Duplicate is a persistent editing tool with the visible instruction Click a clip to duplicate; the clip context-menu Duplicate is the immediate command. Keep consistent tool/action behavior and visible guidance. Initial discovery and repeated-copy steps remain documented friction; no reduction in copy steps is claimed.

precise_trim.response: First end trims sometimes reached 30.134 seconds and a small correction or Properties entry showed 30.000. Record that correction as friction. Preserve snapping, source and Undo semantics and the existing Properties 123 exact-duration route; do not claim every zoomed-out one-drag endpoint is exact. All five final WAVs independently verified as exactly 30.000 seconds.

send_routing_steps.response: Adding a send opens the focused Routing panel and an explicit destination menu. Retain this on-demand location for destination, level and pre/post mode, with adjacent Add bus/Add send mixer entry points. Acknowledge the extra steps; no shorter flow was implemented or claimed in this round.

audio_failure.response: Preserve the repeated stream-failure observations. The prior independent CPAL-only probe reproduced Xrun and the same snd_pcm_avail_delay EIO with injected 60 ms stalls, without RILL code. Default and named output map to the same PCM, and a larger requested buffer was not demonstrated to remedy the failure. The cause of each participant stall remains unknown. Retain fatal handling, Retry/Audio setup and raw diagnostics; no audio product fix, sustained reliability or physical-device conclusion is claimed.

audio_recovery.response: Transport or meter activity after Retry, selecting the named output or subsequent control actions is temporary observed recovery. Repeated later failures remain part of the result. Device selection also recreates the stream and is not a demonstrated remedy; displayed activity does not establish heard audio or sustained healthy playback. The actual sequence needs stream-state evidence before changing restart/error classification.

native_dialog.response: Keep delayed native-picker paint, transient black rectangles and presentation differences in the record. These dialogs run without a window manager; the captures do not isolate an app defect or establish normal desktop behavior. Retain native pickers and require native-desktop reproduction before changing their integration. No rendering or placement fix is claimed.

export_wait.response: Keep asynchronous export, elapsed feedback and explicit completion receipts. The visible wait is a subjective interaction observation; software graphics, virtual audio, screenshot and tool overhead prevent treating session timings as throughput benchmarks. No faster render or completion-time estimate is claimed.

export_percentage.response: The export currently reports elapsed time and completion rather than a percentage. Acknowledge the desire for more progress detail while retaining the existing truthful feedback. These captures show completion, not a stuck export, and do not establish a correctness defect. A percentage indicator would need a separately defined measure across export stages; no percentage feature was added in this iteration.

untested_scope.response: Only the supplied Rill Lab Sine VST3 and the requested task were explored. Broader plug-in compatibility, physical hardware, audible quality and unvisited production features remain untested by these sessions, even where engineering tests exist. Neither absence nor general compatibility can be inferred.

note_press_origin.response: Participant4 logged identical x origins for each three-note chord, but the preserved screenshot shows staggered starts. Source review and unchanged failing regressions confirmed that MIDI press initialization used the latest pointer position instead of the raw primary press position. The correction uses the press position and Shift state for initial focus, hit testing, onset, pitch and gesture origin; later motion and release still use the latest pointer. One unit regression and three app E2Es failed before the fix and pass afterward. Final workspace validation passed 1,447 tests with zero failures and 25 ignored across 261 targets; explicit build, strict Clippy, formatting and whitespace checks also passed. Independent review found no blockers. Original reports, notes and round8 scores remain unchanged; a fresh round9 evaluation is separate.
note_press_origin.attribution_limit: The native screenshots and logged commands corroborate differing onsets; they do not capture exact per-frame native event batching. Source review and regression evidence must establish implementation behavior separately.
note_press_origin.coordinator_confirmation: Root confirmed the source/input defect and assigned tests before a bounded implementation correction.
note_press_origin.separate_endpoint_observation: P4-F4 also reports reducing the clip duration from 56.25 to 56 beats. That endpoint correction is preserved under precise_trim. It is not automatically attributed to the onset bug, and this patch is not claimed to eliminate every snap, release or clip-extension endpoint difference.

validation.independent_code_review: No blockers in raw press-position/Shift initialization, latest-pointer movement/release, existing modal/layer/navigation guards and outside-canvas-origin rejection. This is not a general redesign of out-of-canvas gestures.
validation.explicit_build_strict_clippy_format_whit: passed; evidence in final validation artifact

note_clip_extension.response: Drawing beyond an existing MIDI clip extends it; Participant3 observed a slightly longer result and corrected the edge. Preserve the intended automatic extension and exact Properties duration route. The report does not identify its precise input/grid cause, and the separate onset defect must not automatically be claimed to explain or fix this endpoint observation.

duration_units.response: Participant4 translated 30 seconds into 56 beats at 112 BPM and verified the seconds readout. Clip duration currently edits musical beats with a visible elapsed endpoint; preserve that contract and the mouse keypad. A direct seconds-entry option could reduce this calculation, but no such addition was made or claimed in this iteration.

toolbar_density.response: Participant4 found the toolbars dense while reporting readable, usable controls. Retain explicit mouse-accessible editing tools and contextual help for now. No clipped or unreachable toolbar action was identified in this observation; a density redesign would need to preserve discovery and test the specific affected viewport.

clip_label_readability.response: Short clips at whole-song zoom truncate New pattern to New p..., and Participant5 disliked some small text. Keep clip text inside its own time bounds rather than overlapping adjacent clips; zooming or opening a clip exposes more context and its full editor title. Record the readability preference without claiming a typography fix. Repeated individual duplication is covered separately by the retained Duplicate-tool response.
